stem: Vikram wants to cover a $4$ by $5$ grid of unit squares with $2$ by $1$ tiles. Tiles must not overlap and must not leave gaps.

parts.text: Which claim correctly decides whether the grid can be tiled?

options.text: Yes. The grid has $20$ unit squares, and each column of height $4$ can be filled with two vertical $2$ by $1$ tiles.
No. Any grid with a side of length $5$ cannot be tiled, even when the total number of squares is even.
Yes, because every rectangle of unit squares can be tiled, with no check of area parity or a row-or-column plan.
Call the tiling decision the label unit squares on the grid, and stop there.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: The grid has $20$ squares (even). Height $4$ is even, so each of the five columns can be filled with two vertical $2\times 1$ tiles.

teacher.key_rationale: Even area plus an even side gives an explicit column tiling. Rejecting because one side is $5$, claiming every rectangle tiles, or naming only "unit squares" all miss that hinge.
